$comment: The releases this project measures itself against, and the facts that identify them.
Read by the `Reference releases are intact` step in release-dmg.yml, which fails the
build if any of these tags disappears or moves to a different commit.
GitHub-side tag protection became available when this repository was made public on
2026-08-17 — rulesets need Pro or a public repository, and it is now the latter. This
check is kept alongside rather than replaced by one: a ruleset can stop a tag being
deleted, but it does not record which commit the tag is supposed to point at, nor the
digest of the artifact that was published from it. Those are the facts a fallback point
is actually made of, and they live here.
Four references. v1.0.5 is the floor, v1.0.9 closes the 1.x line, v2.5.11 is the
previous 2.x release and v2.6.0 the current one, published on 2026-09-23. A release
cannot record itself — the commit it names is the commit that carries it, and no file
can contain its own hash — so each entry here is added by the commit after the release
it describes.
v2.6.0 is the first release since 2026-08-30 that did not displace the one before it:
by the owner's decision of 2026-09-23, v2.5.11 stays a reference, and a new release adds
an entry rather than replacing one. The cost the list at three used to name — a fault
introduced recently not bracketed from below by anything nearer than v1.0.9 — is paid
back: v2.5.11 brackets v2.6.0. Before that the list was kept at three, and the release a
new one replaced was withdrawn — release, tag and DMG: v2.5.10 on 2026-09-22, v2.5.9 on
2026-09-20, hours after it was published, v2.5.8 earlier that day, v2.5.7 on 2026-09-13,
through v2.4.0 on 2026-08-30. A reference cannot be re-cut, so the work that follows one
takes a number of its own. Whether a release that follows v2.6.0 retires anything is a
decision rather than a consequence of publishing.
Adding or changing any value below is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff as one.

references.why: First release of the numbering that survives; everything before it was withdrawn.
The second reference: credits the corpus authors, bounds a download that had nothing but the disk to stop it, and is the recent state to fall back to rather than the floor.

The third reference, and the release before v2.6.0, which did not retire it. It replaced v2.5.10, and unlike that one it carries code: the inventory's search field is labelled in English, a CTH group is one run even when its labels share a number, a dropped BOM is counted under DROP_BOM, and two cache tests no longer leave a working directory in TMPDIR. The package it builds hashes to dfe12b37…adff over 23 940 files, the byte mirror to the unchanged 7cfcdce4…35d0 over 23 936 documents in 663 folders. It is the first release whose binary is reproducible across machines: the application the runner built, 4e2786bc…a594, is byte-for-byte the one the owner's machine builds from the same commit, because the release build remaps the building machine's paths, keeps the debug map out of LC_UUID, and holds Xcode 15.2 (SDK 14.2) and Node 22.23.2 on both sides. Revisions 80 and 81.

The current release and the fourth reference, added beside v2.5.11 rather than in its place. Each CTH heading of the inventory carries the catalogue's title for its number; the download's read timeout is in force, 30 s, and a cancel reaches a silent server within it; a body the server cut short is a network failure, not a disk one; a declared XML version other than 1.0 is refused; the search hint writes its numbers the English way on any machine; the window is granted core:default and dialog:allow-open only and the store plugin is gone. The package it builds hashes to 83392544…3dc99 over 23 941 files, the byte mirror to the unchanged 7cfcdce4…35d0. The application the runner built, e9fcdb38…3aea, is byte-for-byte the one two local builds of the same commit gave on the owner's machine. Revisions 86 and 87.
